subject: SIG evidence parity check: outstanding items for HealthBridge SIG
body:
From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@healthbridge.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: security@healthbridge.com
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SIG packet — outstanding items and format question

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood’s platform yesterday. Our InfoSec team started a SIG validation and we pulled what we have from the portal — thanks for the quick access. We still need a few artifacts to complete our review for the procurement window next week:

- The most recent SOC 2 Type II report (PDF, ideally the auditor cover page + AICPA attestation).
- A short (1–2 page) penetration test summary highlighting high/critical findings and remediation status (we can accept a redacted executive summary).
- ISO statements or cert status for 27001 / 27701 if available.
- A security overview deck we can share with our internal legal and procurement teams.

One question — do you have a single mapping table that ties SIG questions to the delivered evidence (we call it an evidence-parity matrix)? That would speed our sign-off. If you can send those items by EOD Monday (Oct 4), we should be able to finish the SIG evaluation and move to contract.

Thanks,
Sarah
Security Program Manager
HealthBridge Systems

-----

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@healthbridge.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG packet — outstanding items and format question

Sarah — thanks for the clear list.

Quick status from our side: we have the SOC 2 Type II 2026 PDF and the ISO27001 status statement ready. The pen test vendor provided a detailed report that contains client IPs and contract references; we can produce a redacted executive summary that omits sensitive infrastructure details (attached: pen_test_summary_redacted.pdf). I’ve attached a concise security deck geared toward procurement and legal.

On the evidence-parity matrix: we maintain a single sheet that maps SIG sections to artifact filenames and page references. I’ll attach the matrix as a small CSV and also paste a quick inline map below for the handful of items you asked about. If you prefer a Google Sheet access link instead of attachments, say the word and we’ll share it.

Attachments in this reply (stubs):
- Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2026.pdf (auditor attestation page included)
- pen_test_summary_redacted.pdf ( executive summary )
- ISO27001_statement.pdf (current scope statement)
- Security_Deck_for_HealthBridge_v2.pdf (10 slides)
- sig_evidence_parity_matrix.csv (maps SIG section -> artifact)

Inline mapping (excerpt):
- SIG-1 (Org & Governance) -> Security_Deck_for_HealthBridge_v2.pdf (slides 2-4)
- SIG-5 (Encryption) -> Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2026.pdf (Control A.8.3.2)
- SIG-9 (Vulnerability Mgmt) -> pen_test_summary_redacted.pdf (Executive Summary)
- SIG-12 (Certifications) -> ISO27001_statement.pdf

We will also:
- Share a read-only Google Sheet for the full parity matrix by Monday morning.
- Send a DocuSign link for the standard redaction/non-disclosure attestation for the pen test memo if HealthBridge needs it for procurement.

Let me know if you want the full SOC 2 binder under NDA; otherwise the attestation + relevant pages should be sufficient.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Security & Compliance (Solutions)
Redwood Inference

-----

From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@healthbridge.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG packet — outstanding items and format question

Mateo — this is great and on a tight timeline, much appreciated. A couple of notes from our InfoSec:

- The redacted pen test summary looks fine; can you include the remediation status (open / in-progress / closed) for each finding in a two-column appendix? No IPs needed, just the finding id and status.
- For the SOC 2, procurement wants the cover page + opinion paragraph; legal may ask for the full report under NDA — please send the NDA link if you have a standard template.
- We prefer a Google Sheet parity mapping. Please share read-only and give healthbridge.com domain access.

If we get these artifacts and the parity mapping by EOD Monday we’ll slot Redwood for contract review on Tuesday.

Thanks — Sarah

-----

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@healthbridge.com>
Cc: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG packet — outstanding items and format question

Sarah — sending the Google Sheet now and attaching the updated pen test appendix with remediation statuses. Also including a one-click DocuSign link to our standard mutual NDA (redaction access + pen-test handling). Links below.

Drive parity sheet (read-only): https://drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2b3c-redwood-healthbridge-evidence
DocuSign NDA: https://www.docusign.com/transaction/ABC-HealthBridge-123

Attachments in this message (stubs): pen_test_summary_redacted.pdf (with appendix), sig_evidence_parity_matrix.csv

If you want a quick 15-min sync to walk procurement/legal through mapping and what to expect in the SOC 2 binder, Mateo and I are available Tuesday 9:00–11:00 PT.

Warmly,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

-----

From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@healthbridge.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 14:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG packet — outstanding items and format question

Confirmed receipt of attachments and links — the parity sheet looks complete. Procurement scheduled the contract review for Tuesday 10:30 PT; I’ll invite Redwood to the meeting if you can join. We’ll follow up on the full SOC 2 under NDA after the meeting.

Appreciate the rapid turnaround.

— Sarah
Security Program Manager
HealthBridge Systems
